article_title: Engaging ESP University Students in Flipped Classrooms for Developing Functional Writing Skills, HOTs, and Eliminating Writer's Block
citation: Salem, A. A. M. S. (2018). Engaging ESP University Students in Flipped Classrooms for Developing Functional Writing Skills, HOTs, and Eliminating Writer's Block. English Language Teaching, 11(12). https://doi.org/10.5539/elt.v11n12p177
title: Functional Writing Skills Test (FWST) for business ESP students
description: The FWST is a 100-point standardized instrument built for the study to assess the writing performance of business English students, with "four main sections; writing business reports & Proposals, writing business emails, writing agenda & minutes, and writing CVs & Resumes", 25 points each. It uses multiple-choice, open-ended and essay (free writing) questions and was designed to depend on web-based tools to match the flipped approach. The article reports Cronbach's alpha coefficients for the sections ranging from .558 to .714 (standardized-item alphas .968 to .981) and internal consistency coefficients supporting its validity.
requirements: Reliability and internal-consistency evidence, as reported in Tables 1 and 2, to rely on the test as a measure of functional writing skills
constraints: The test was designed for business majors in the banking section at the College of Management Sciences
target_learners: third-year undergraduate business majors studying ESP
target_learning_goals: functional writing skills for university study and the workplace
examples: The examination for the course's first part comprised a multiple-choice digital exam in the Moodle learning management system.
